title: role-entry-minimal-friction-checklist-7-day-experiment
content:
Quick context

Purpose: run a small, low-friction onboarding experiment for ICs (engineer and product) to validate whether a curated 7-day entry path reduces time-to-first-meaningful-PR and improves confidence. This doc is intentionally compact — actionable checklists, clear owners, and measurable short signals.

Audience: hiring managers, buddy engineers, people-ops, IT provisioning, security.

Success metrics (what we'll measure):
- Time to first merged PR (target: <= 7 days for contributor-level tasks)
- % of hires who self-report "can ship a small change" by day 7 (target: >= 75%)
- Access defects logged (target: <= 2 blocking access tickets in first 7 days)
- Hiring signal: first code review feedback -> hiring manager confidence score (post-7d survey)

High-level constraints and assumptions:
- Experiment scope: new hires in teams with maintained starter microtasks and an assigned buddy. Not for managers or infra-heavy roles.
- Provisioning window: IT aims to complete core access within 24 hours; anything longer flags a follow-up.
- Minimal training: no formal classroom sessions in week 1; rely on written playbook + buddy pairing.

Roles & ownership (single lines):
- People Ops: create offer-to-day0 checklist, schedule orientation, send welcome email template (owner: Marisol).
- IT/Access: provisioning core accounts (owner: Ben Hsu).
- Hiring Manager: assign buddy, pick 2 microtasks, set expectation call day 1 (owner: hiring manager).
- Buddy: daily 30-min sync day1-5, review first PR, triage questions (owner: assigned buddy).

Day-by-day checklist (minimal friction)
- Day -1 (pre-arrival)
  - People Ops: send welcome email with Day 1 agenda, first-week microtask links, Slack channel invite, campus map/parking (if relevant).
  - IT: create accounts, order laptop or confirm ship, create calendar invites for W1 synces.
  - Hiring Manager: assign buddy + share 1-sentence team context with buddy.

- Day 0 (when hardware arrives / remote onboarding afternoon)
  - New hire: unbox laptop, run setup script, join Slack + SSO, confirm calendar and payroll docs.
  - IT: confirm VPN/KMS access for private deployments (if needed).
  - People Ops: 20-min welcome intro (culture, org chart, time-off basics).

- Day 1
  - 30-min manager touch: team priorities + expectations, show codebase map.
  - Buddy: 30-min pairing & repo walkthrough.
  - New hire: complete small environment smoke test (run unit tests locally).
  - Microtask #1 assigned (tweak README or small lint fix). Aim: merge within 48h.

- Day 2-3
  - Buddy daily 30-min office hours; review progress.
  - New hire works on microtask #1; submit PR with description, test, and a short note on follow-ups.
  - Hiring manager: short async check-in if blockers persist.

- Day 4-5
  - Microtask #2 assigned (instrumentation, small bug, or docs-driven change). Target: second PR merged by day 7.
  - Buddy conducts light code review coaching session (how to read diffs, respond to feedback).

- Day 6-7
  - Finalize onboarding checklist: update personal notes, add to team onboarding doc any missing steps.
  - Post-7-day survey link sent (1-2 min, quick scale on confidence/access/issues).
  - Hiring manager fills short confidence rubric and schedules 15-min calibration if score < 3/5.

Access & provisioning quick rules
- Minimum accounts to be verified by day 1: Slack, GitHub access (team repo read/write), CI runner token, internal docs read, payroll.
- Private deployment customers: require KMS token and test VPC access; flagged to security on day 0.
- If any of the core access items are not provisioned within 24 hours post-arrival, IT must open a JIRA ticket and tag people-ops.

Condensed interview/hiring rubric for early signal alignment (used by hiring manager post-7d)
- Areas (score 1-5): Code comprehension (reads diffs quickly), Practical ownership (completes microtask to shipping), Communication (clarity in PR and async), Collaboration (responds to review), SLO-awareness (asks about reliability/cost when relevant).
- Minimal passing signal: >=3 in at least 4/5 areas OR manager note that trajectory is clearly positive with a remediation plan.

Microtask design guidelines (for hiring managers & eng leads)
- Should be small but meaningful: <8 hours estimated, touches common workflow (PR, CI, revert), includes automated test where feasible.
- Prefer two microtasks that increase in scope (README -> small bug/fix -> small feature).
- Include a short "context" note and links to relevant docs; include expected reviewer(s).

Survey & feedback (post-7d)
- One-question hire survey: "Do you feel able to ship a small change independently?" (yes/no) + optional 1-2 sentence freeform.
- Manager rubic submission: quick form with numeric fields and 1-line rationale.
- People Ops compiles results weekly for experiment cohort; we will run N=30 hires before deciding on wider rollout.

Failure modes & contingency
- Laptop delayed: fallback is remote dev container + temporary loaner (IT to coordinate).
- Access denied to private resources: escalates to security with SLA 48h for non-prod access.
- Buddy bandwidth: if buddy unavailable, manager must nominally provide 4h coverage across week.

Open questions (to resolve before pilot):
- Which teams are eligible? Proposal: product infra, frontend, backend feature teams. Exclude infra-oncall heavy roles.
- What incentives for buddies? Idea: 1.25x mentorship credit for engineering review capacity (tracking via weekly rewards).
- How to log microtask difficulty consistently? Proposal: 3-point scale in the microtask template.

TODOs (owners and quick dates)
- Finalize microtask template (owner: Liam) — due 2025-03-12.
- IT: create a day0 provisioning checklist and a one-click provisioning request form (owner: Ben) — due 2025-03-19.
- People Ops: draft the welcome email and add experiment opt-in checkbox in offer flow (owner: Marisol) — due 2025-03-05 (WIP).
- Product: identify first 10 hires for pilot cohort (owner: Priya) — due 2025-03-20.

Notes to self / rough ideas (keep informal)
- Could run A/B with standard onboarding vs minimal friction and track differences in week 3 churn.
- Consider shipping a tiny "first day" badge in Slack to prompt buddy intros.
- We should instrument time-to-merge as a metric inside our internal analytics pipeline (ask data infra).

Appendix: quick welcome email template (editable)
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — Day 1 agenda & quick links
Hi [Name],
Welcome to Redwood — excited to have you! Quick notes for Day 1:
- Slack invite: [link]
- Day 1 call with manager: [calendar link]
- Repo starter guide: [link]
- Microtask #1: [link] (target: merge in 48h)
If anything is missing when you sign in, ping #it-help or reply to this email and I will triage. — Marisol

End of doc.
